context.firstUser: A teacher, streamer, coach, or group host who wants every fair selection to feel like a shared event.
context.primaryJob: Recognize NameSnap immediately, run a numbered random draw, and give repeat winners visibly different high-energy celebrations.
context.desiredResponse: The icon should read as NameSnap rather than a wheel or calendar, and the celebration library should feel varied, joyful, coherent, and legible on both phone and desktop.
referenceProducts: Wheel of Names — clear live-draw context and result emphasis
Kahoot — high-energy group feedback and readable result states, without copying its visual identity

blurTest.evidence: At gallery scale, the contestant-list icon, warm winner token, white result card, black event backdrop, and saturated character art remain distinct without reading labels.

silhouetteTest.evidence: The working app retains its producer-panel plus live-stage silhouette; the celebration becomes an unmistakable full-screen poster with a deliberately oversized character.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: The header identifies NameSnap with the new list-to-winner icon, while the winner screen communicates the selected number, selected name, celebration variant, and next actions immediately.

realityTest.evidence: Rendered states use an eight-person numbered roster and a recalled Tom Holland winner, with actual recent-pick, no-repeat, and reset controls rather than a decorative mock screen.

journeyTest.evidence: The same numbered winner and NameSnap token system continue from setup through live stage to celebration on phone and desktop.

platformTest.evidence: The 390×844 render preserves readable winner copy and touch targets; the 1440×1000 render scales the art dramatically without obscuring the result card; the 32×32 icon stays recognizable.

buyerValueTest.evidence: Thirty hero subjects multiplied by five palettes and two directions provide 300 distinct celebration presentations, reducing repetition during classrooms, streams, and recurring giveaways.

implementationTest.evidence: All thirty hero assets resolve in production code, all twenty new PNGs have genuine alpha, matching files ship in web and native bundles, the 300-count contract is regression-tested, and both web and iOS builds pass.

screenFindings.finding: At phone size, the list-and-crowned-winner icon remains distinct in the compact header and the tactile setup hierarchy remains intact.
At desktop size, the icon anchors the brand while the working contestant panel and stage occupy the first viewport without marketing-frame leakage.
The new gamer character reads clearly above the phone result card; the number, winner name, explanation, dismissal, and reset controls remain unobstructed.
The same character becomes intentionally theatrical on desktop while the centered card remains the primary information surface.
The redesigned icon survives favicon scale: contestant cards and crowned winner token remain perceptible with no wheel, numeral, or calendar cue.

independentCritic.categoryFluency: PASS — numbered pool, fair selection, no-repeat state, recent winner, and an emphatic result moment are specific to the product category.
independentCritic.originality: PASS — the inked sticker characters, crayon texture, lavender hard shadows, gold winner token, and roster-derived icon form a recognizable NameSnap world without tracing a reference.
independentCritic.marketingFrameLeakage: PASS — the evaluated initial view is the actual working picker, and the celebration is a functional result state rather than a landing-page mockup.
independentCritic.importedCliches: PASS — common celebration subjects are translated into the established NameSnap illustration language; the icon depicts the app's real list-to-winner mechanic instead of a generic roulette wheel.
independentCritic.adversarialFinding: Several first-pass generations contained baked checkerboards and one acrobat remained contaminated after two extraction attempts. Those outputs were rejected; each accepted file was re-inspected at original scale and programmatically confirmed to contain real alpha before integration.

repairs: Replaced the web favicon, PWA icon, Apple touch icon, metadata icon, and header identity with the same contestant-list-to-crowned-winner artwork used by the redesigned native app.
Prepared a separate 512×512 Gravatar-ready export from the same identity artwork.
Added twenty new celebration subjects and integrated matching transparent files into both the web and native asset bundles.
Expanded the deterministic hero system from 100 to 300 visual combinations.
Rejected contaminated background-removal results and replaced the failed acrobat concept with a clean juggler asset.
Added automated coverage for every celebration file, the 300-variation contract, manifest icon declarations, and Gravatar export.
verdict: PASS — the redesigned web identity and expanded celebration library clear the rendered quality floor at favicon, phone, and desktop scales with no known missing art, fake transparency, wheel mismatch, calendar cue, clipping, or build failure.
